docs.title: Compiled list of user Needs
docs.text: After reviewing the 100 user needs gathered from benchmark products, the team organized the needs into categories based on common user requirements. A meta-need was created for each category to represent the overall goal of that group. The individual needs were then prioritized as High, Medium, or Low based on repeated customer feedback, importance to the primary function of the automatic dog food dispenser, and team judgment.

docs.title: Prioritization Process
docs.text:
The team prioritized the user needs using three levels: High, Medium, and Low. The rankings were based on the frequency of similar comments found during benchmarking, the importance of each need to the primary function of the automatic dog food dispenser, and team judgment.

High-priority needs represent requirements that directly affect the dispenser's ability to provide reliable, safe, and consistent feeding. Medium-priority needs improve usability, maintenance, compatibility, and convenience. Low-priority needs provide additional benefits to the user but are less critical to the primary function of the product.

docs.title: Project Objective
docs.text: This project aims to investigate and develop an automatic pet food dispenser that provides pet owners with a convenient, reliable, and consistent way to feed their pets. The product will be designed to dispense predetermined portions of pet food at scheduled times, reducing the need for owners to manually feed their pets throughout the day. The primary objective is to develop a user-friendly, programmable automatic feeding system that can accommodate the daily routines of pet owners while supporting the nutritional needs of pets. The dispenser will incorporate a timer-based feeding system that allows users to establish feeding schedules able to be customized to consumer need. Depending on the final design and available resources, additional features may include adjustable portion sizes, a food storage container, a manual feeding button, and indicators for low food levels or cleaning and maintenance. The intended outcome is a functional prototype that demonstrates the ability to automatically dispense pet food according to a user-defined schedule. The prototype will be evaluated based on its dispensing accuracy, scheduling performance, ease of use, reliability, and safety for pets and pet owners alike.

docs.title: Stakeholders
docs.text:
• Target group Pet owners who have busy or unpredictable schedules and want to maintain a consistent feeding routine for their pets. This includes working professionals, students, frequent travelers, and owners who may not always be home during their pet's normal feeding times.
  • Target purchaser Pet owners and household members responsible for purchasing pet-care products and taking care of household pets that have busy schedules, long periods away from home, or travel frequently.
  • Customer service Prefers a product that is simple to troubleshoot, clean, refill, and maintain with accurate timing and dispensing capabilities.
  • Marketing & Sales division Looks for unique selling points centered around convenience, reliable automatic feeding, portion control, and ease of use.
  • Retailers Prefer a product that is compact, durable, easy to package, and capable of withstanding normal transportation and storage conditions, as well as state clearly the product's main features, intended pet types, feeding capacity, and ease of use to potential customers to help drive sales.

docs.title: User Story #1: Working Pet Owner
docs.text:
Jordan is a 29-year-old engineer who works full-time and is usually away from home for most of the day. His dog is normally fed twice a day, once in the morning and again in the evening. However, meetings, traffic, and changes in his work schedule sometimes prevent him from getting home at the dog's normal feeding time.

Before leaving for work, Jordan fills the automatic pet food dispenser and programs the desired feeding schedule and portion size. At the scheduled time, the dispenser automatically releases the predetermined portion of food without requiring Jordan to be home or interact with the device. When Jordan returns, he can check the remaining food supply and refill the dispenser when necessary.

The automatic dispenser allows Jordan to maintain a consistent feeding routine for his dog even when his own schedule changes. It also reduces the need to rely on another person to feed the dog when he is unexpectedly away from home.

docs.title: User Story #2: Pet Owner Away for the Day
docs.text:
Maya is a college student who occasionally spends an entire day away from her apartment because of classes, work, and other activities. Her schedule varies throughout the week, but she wants her dog to continue receiving food at consistent times and in consistent portions regardless of when she returns home.

Before leaving for the day, Maya checks that the dispenser contains enough food and adjusts the programmed feeding times if necessary. The dispenser stores the food securely so her dog cannot access additional food between meals. At each scheduled feeding time, it automatically dispenses the selected portion. If Maya's schedule changes on another day, she can modify the feeding schedule to match her dog's routine.

This allows Maya to spend longer periods away from home while maintaining her dog's normal feeding schedule. The adjustable schedule and automatic portioning also reduce the possibility of missed, delayed, or inconsistent feedings.

docs.title: Aspects
docs.text: The automatic pet food dispenser will be designed based on the following requirements. The P1 - P10 is the "code" to indicate the priority of the requirement, from low to high.

docs.title: 1. Hardware / Product Design
docs.text:
• 1.1 The product shall have a container that can store enough pet food for multiple feedings. (P9)
  • 1.2 The product shall dispense food without regularly getting jammed. (P10)
  • 1.3 The product shall be stable enough that a pet cannot easily knock it over. (P8)
  • 1.4 The food container shall be easy for the owner to refill. (P8)

docs.title: 2. Software / Functionality
docs.text:
• 2.1 The product shall allow the user to set specific feeding times. (P10)
  • 2.2 The product shall automatically dispense food at the scheduled time. (P10)
  • 2.3 The product shall dispense a consistent amount of food for each feeding. (P9)
  • 2.4 The product shall have a manual button that allows the user to dispense food when needed. (P7)

docs.title: 3. Interactivity & User Experience
docs.text:
• 3.1 The product shall be simple for the user to set up and operate. (P9)
  • 3.2 The user shall be able to easily change the feeding schedule. (P9)
  • 3.3 The product shall be easy to refill and clean. (P8)
  • 3.4 The product shall clearly show the user when it is operating or dispensing food. (P6)

docs.title: 4. Customization
docs.text:
• 4.1 The user shall be able to choose different feeding times. (P10)
  • 4.2 The user shall be able to select different portion sizes. (P8)
  • 4.3 The product shall allow more than one feeding to be scheduled per day. (P9)
  • 4.4 The product shall work with common types and sizes of dry pet food. (P7)

docs.title: 5. Manufacturing
docs.text:
• 5.1 The product shall use parts that are available within the team's project budget. (P9)
  • 5.2 The product shall be designed using materials and manufacturing methods available to the team. (P8)
  • 5.3 The product shall be simple enough for the team to assemble and troubleshoot. (P8)
  • 5.4 Major components shall be replaceable if they become damaged. (P6)

docs.title: 6. Safety
docs.text:
• 6.1 The product shall keep electrical components covered and away from the pet. (P10)
  • 6.2 The pet shall not be able to easily reach the moving parts of the dispensing mechanism. (P10)
  • 6.3 The product shall not have exposed sharp edges that could harm the pet or owner. (P10)
  • 6.4 The product shall operate within the safe voltage and current limits of its electrical components. (P10)

docs.title: Requirement Criteria Specifications
docs.text:
• 1.1.1 - Regulate system power from 9 volts to 5 volts. (Test)
  • 1.1.2 - Keep the system current below 1.5 amps during normal operation. (Test)
  • 1.2.1 - The dispenser should complete 10 feeding cycles without the food getting jammed. (Test)
  • 2.1.1 - The user should be able to program at least two different feeding times per day. (Demonstration)
  • 2.2.1 - The dispenser should activate within 1 minute of the scheduled feeding time. (Test)
  • 2.3.1 - The amount of food dispensed should stay within 10% of the selected portion over 5 feeding tests. (Test)
  • 3.1.1 - The user should be able to set or change the feeding schedule using the controls on the dispenser. (Demonstration)
  • 3.3.1 - The food container should be removable or accessible for refilling and cleaning without special tools. (Inspection)
  • 5.1.1 - The parts used for the prototype should stay within the team's project budget. (Analysis)
  • 6.1.1 - Electrical and moving components should not be exposed where the pet can easily reach them during normal use. (Inspection)

docs.title: Open Questions
docs.text:
• What dispensing method will work best without the food getting stuck?
  • How much food should the dispenser be able to hold?
  • What portion sizes should the user be able to choose from?
  • Should the dispenser save the feeding schedule if it loses power?
  • What is the best way to make the dispenser easy to refill and clean?

docs.title: Intro/overview
docs.text:
The goal of this ideation process was to generate a wide variety of possible features for our automatic dog food dispenser. Our team used the user needs identified during the Voice of the Customer benchmarking process as the foundation for the brainstorm. The benchmarking process produced 100 organized user needs covering dispensing performance, scheduling and controls, reliability, food storage, ease of use, maintenance, food protection, power, pet interaction, and physical design. These needs were prioritized as High, Medium, or Low based on repeated customer feedback, importance to the primary function of the dispenser, and team judgment.

For the ideation process, we focused primarily on the High priority needs while also including Medium and Low priority needs when they provided opportunities to improve the overall user experience. The purpose of the brainstorm was to generate individual features that could later be combined into different complete product concepts.

The groups were reviewed to identify which features were most important to the overall product experience. The highest ranked features were those that directly affected reliable food dispensing, ease of use, food storage, reliability, and the pet's interaction with the dispenser.

docs.text:
After sorting the features, the team discussed which ideas would have the greatest effect on the primary function of the product. Features were ranked within each group based on their importance to reliable feeding, ease of use, maintenance, food protection, and pet interaction.

Group Rank Feature Reason for High Ranking Dispensing & Portion Control 1 Anti-jam mechanism A jam could prevent the pet from receiving food at the scheduled time. 2 Portion control settings Allows the owner to control how much food is dispensed. 3 Programmable timer Allows automatic feeding without requiring the owner to be present. 4 Jam detection sensor Can identify a dispensing problem before it prevents normal operation. 5 Food agitator Helps keep food moving toward the dispensing mechanism. Scheduling & User Controls 1 Setup wizard Makes initial programming easier for users. 2 Nonvolatile memory Preserves feeding settings during a power interruption. 3 Editable feeding schedule Allows users to change individual feeding times as needed. 4 Status display Gives the user information about the current operating state. 5 Error code display Helps the user identify and troubleshoot problems. docs.title: 3.4 Three Distinct Product Concepts
docs.text: The next stage was to collect the strongest features into three different product concepts. Features were intentionally recombined so that each concept emphasizes a different approach to solving the user's needs.

docs.text:
Primary Focus: Precision, automation, and user control.

The Smart Precision Feeder emphasizes accurate portioning and advanced programming. It is designed for users who want detailed control over feeding schedules and portions.

Design Goal: Provide precise, programmable feeding while giving the owner clear information about the dispenser's current status.

docs.title: Concept 2: Reliable Away from Home Feeder

Primary Focus: Reliability and independent operation.

The Reliable Away from Home Feeder emphasizes dependable operation when the owner is not available. The design combines mechanical reliability, food storage, and backup power.

The Pet Friendly Modular Feeder emphasizes the physical experience of the pet and the owner's ability to maintain and adapt the product.

Features that were not selected for one of the three primary concepts were not discarded. They remain available as a separate pool of ideas that can be revisited during concept development.

Examples include:

  • Divided storage compartment

  • Modern enclosure

  • Visual instructions
  • Replaceable components
  • Portable design

Keeping these features available allows the team to incorporate additional ideas if the concepts are modified during the next stage.

docs.title: Brainstorming Process
docs.text:
The team began the ideation process by reviewing the user needs and product requirements identified during the previous benchmarking assignment. The brainstorming session focused on generating a large number of possible product features for an automatic pet food dispenser without immediately judging or eliminating ideas. The goal was to explore a wide range of possible solutions that could address the needs of both the pet and the owner. The team members participated in the brainstorming and discussed possible features based on the requirements identified during the benchmarking process. Ideas were collected and organized into the team's working document so that the features could be reviewed and modified after the initial brainstorming session. The team used the project GitHub document to record the ideas and organize the results. This allowed the brainstormed features to be preserved and easily reorganized during the later stages of the ideation process.

The primary source used to generate the requirements was the Voice of the Customer Benchmarking assignment. That assignment examined five benchmark products: a timed medicine dispenser, an automatic paper towel dispenser, an automatic pet food dispenser, a gumball dispenser, and a double cereal dispenser. The user needs identified from these products provided the foundation for the brainstorming session. The requirements were organized around areas such as dispensing performance, scheduling and controls, reliability, food storage and capacity, ease of use, cleaning and maintenance, food protection, power, pet interaction, and physical design. The team also used the benchmark products and their identified features as inspiration for generating additional ideas. Instead of limiting the brainstorm to features already found in the benchmark products, the team combined and modified existing ideas to create possible improvements for the pet food dispenser. This resulted in 100 potential product features across five major categories.

docs.title: Grouping and Ranking Features
docs.text:
After the initial brainstorm was completed, the features were sorted into five thematic groups: 1. Dispensing & Portion Control, 2. Scheduling & User Controls, 3. Storage, Food Protection & Capacity, 4. Reliability, Maintenance & Power, and 5. Pet Interaction, Stability & Physical Design. The features were grouped according to the primary function they served or the user need they addressed. This made it easier to identify patterns within the brainstorm and compare features that solved similar problems. The team then reviewed the features within each group and identified the ideas that were most important to the overall product. Ranking was based primarily on how directly each feature supported the main purpose of the automatic pet food dispenser, how much it addressed an important user need, and how much it could improve reliability, usability, safety, or the pet's experience. For example, features such as anti-jam mechanisms, portion control, programmable scheduling, backup power, large-capacity storage, and stable physical construction were identified as important because they directly affect the dispenser's ability to provide food reliably.

The ranking process also provided an opportunity to combine existing ideas into new features. The anti-jam mechanism, jam detection sensor, and reverse motor were combined into an Automatic Jam Recovery System. Another example was the backup battery, nonvolatile memory, and automatic feeding schedule were combined into a Power-Loss Recovery System. These combinations allowed the team to develop new ideas from the strongest features identified during the discussion. The highest ranked and newly generated features were recombined into three different product concepts: the Smart Precision Feeder, the Reliable Away from Home Feeder, and the Pet Friendly Modular Feeder. Features that were not selected for one of the three concepts were retained separately rather than discarded so they could be reconsidered during future concept development.
